# KOL Campaigns Need More Than Impression Screenshots

Source: https://lowob.com/research/web3-kol-campaign-measurement/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-08-16 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Growth

> Summary: An impression screenshot proves a post was delivered. It does not prove anyone understood the product, connected a wallet or came back. Buy a defined behaviour, not a follower count; instrument the path from click to on-chain action before the campaign starts; judge each creator on distribution, activation, durability and economics; and make the second payment conditional on evidence. Disclosure belongs in the same brief: the FTC, the SEC, the UK FCA and MiCA all treat a paid crypto post as advertising.

## Key points

- Reach is visible; commercial impact is harder to prove, so most KOL reports stop at reach.
- Choose the behaviour first: wallet connection and deposit, a developer integration trial, or an institutional conversation each need a different creator.
- The measurement gap sits between the click and the wallet; plan attribution before paying for distribution.
- A wallet is not a person and a connection is not a customer; one airdrop farmer ran over 20,000 accounts.
- Undisclosed paid promotion is a legal risk, not only a reputational one: the SEC fined a celebrity $1 million for an undisclosed paid crypto post.

Reach is visible. Commercial impact is usually harder to prove. That asymmetry is why so many creator reports in crypto are folders of impression screenshots and launch-day charts. The useful question is narrower: did this creator bring a relevant audience to a specific action, and did that behaviour persist after the campaign ended? This is as much a buying problem as a tracking problem. A team can commission a campaign before defining whom it needs to reach, what the audience should do, or how the result will be measured. This piece is part of our hub on [building a community that lasts](https://lowob.com/research/building-a-community-that-lasts/), because a KOL campaign that brings the wrong people in makes the community's job harder.

## KOL is the default. That does not make it effective

Paid creator promotion is one of the most common acquisition formats in crypto, and spend tends to cluster around launches and major events rather than recurring budgets. That concentrates the whole explanation of a product into one window, and judges it on one spike. A widely adopted channel can still be poorly measured.

This is not an argument against KOL partnerships. Focused technical creators, educators and researchers can explain a product better than the team can, to an audience that trusts them. Our piece on the difference between [influencers, creators, KOLs and ambassadors](https://lowob.com/research/influencer-creator-kol-ambassador/) sets out the formats. The argument is against judging success by a screenshot.

## Define the job before choosing the voice

Set the intended outcome first. A staking product might need users to connect a wallet and delegate. An infrastructure team might need credible developers to try an integration. A tokenised-asset provider might need informed conversations with a small set of decision makers. Those are different jobs. Each needs a different audience, a different landing page and a different measure.

Creator selection follows the job. Check who actually engages with the creator, the questions their audience asks, whether the creator understands the product well enough to explain it, and any sponsorship conflicts with competing projects. A focused technical creator may deliver fewer views and more valuable actions than a larger generalist account.

## Connect the click to the action

The main measurement gap is between a click and later wallet behaviour. Standard web analytics record visits but do not automatically link them to on-chain actions. Consider a user who clicks a creator's link, leaves, returns two days later on another device, connects a wallet and deposits. Linking that deposit to the creator requires campaign context to survive the gap, and it often does not: device changes, cleared browser data and privacy settings all break the chain.

So plan measurement before launch. Give each creator a unique link, preserve campaign context through wallet connection where users consent to it, and track the first meaningful action and later behaviour. Our explainer on [lead source attribution](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-lead-source-attribution/) covers the general mechanics; the crypto-specific step is carrying the source across the wallet connection.

Then evaluate in four stages.

| Check | What it measures | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distribution | Qualified views, referral visits, audience relevance | Did the message reach people who might use the product? |
| Activation | Attributed wallet connections, first deposits, swaps or other product actions | Did a referral become meaningful product use? |
| Durability | 7-day and 30-day cohorts, repeat actions, retained value | Did activity continue after the campaign ended? |
| Economics | Full channel spend divided by verified activated users, compared with alternatives | Is there evidence to invest in this creator again? |

Be honest about what the numbers are. A wallet is not necessarily a person: academic analysis of airdrops documents a single farmer operating over 20,000 accounts on one network. A connection is not necessarily a customer. Attribution is often partial, so state which outcomes are observed, which are inferred and which are unknown. A useful KOL report should make it possible to cut, renew or redesign the next campaign. If it only proves content was delivered, it is a fulfilment report.

Illustrative example: two creators, one budget

Decision
:   Renew Creator B for a second, smaller test and pause Creator A, despite A's larger reach.

Reason and owner
:   Creator A drove 400 wallet connections, of which 12% completed a first transaction and 18% were active at 30 days. Creator B drove 150 connections, of which 31% completed a first transaction and 34% were active at 30 days. First transactions were roughly equal, around 48 and 46, but B's users stayed. Owned by the growth lead.

What changed
:   Before the renewal, the team checked deposit size, repeat use and the full cost of each creator, not only the fee.

Illustrative: adapted from an illustrative comparison published by an on-chain analytics vendor; not a client case study or a reported campaign result.

## Price the full cost of acquisition

Creator fees are only part of the cost. Include briefing, strategy, editing, management, event support, incentives, data tooling and moderation of the traffic that arrives. Compare KOLs with other channels on the same basis: partnerships, founder-led education, organic research content, affiliates and paid media.

Cost per activated wallet is more useful than cost per click, but only when paired with retention, wallet quality and downstream value. Otherwise a campaign optimised for activation can simply purchase the cheapest one-time action. The discipline is the same as any [campaign test that reaches a decision](https://lowob.com/research/campaign-testing-that-reaches-a-decision/): decide in advance what result would justify more spend, and what would end it. Our piece on [attribution vs incrementality](https://lowob.com/research/attribution-vs-incrementality/) covers the harder question of whether the creator caused the action or only touched it.

> Buy a defined behaviour, not a creator's follower count, and make the second payment conditional on evidence.

## Disclosure is part of the brief

A paid creator post about a token is advertising in every major jurisdiction, and the brief should say so before the post is written.

| Jurisdiction | Rule | What it means for a KOL brief |
| --- | --- | --- |
| US, FTC | Endorsement Guides, 16 CFR 255.5 | A material connection the audience would not expect must be disclosed "clearly and conspicuously": difficult to miss and easily understood |
| US, SEC | Anti-touting provision | Where the token is a security, promoters must disclose the nature, source and amount of compensation; the SEC's 2022 case over an undisclosed $250,000 post ended in a $1.26 million settlement |
| UK, FCA | FG24/1 and the cryptoasset promotions regime | Influencers can be caught without direct payment if they have a commercial interest; firms remain responsible for promotions they cause to be made; breach can be a criminal offence |
| EU, MiCA | Article 7 | Marketing communications must be clearly identifiable as such, fair, clear and not misleading, and consistent with the white paper |

The US position on which tokens are securities shifted in 2026, with the SEC's March interpretation placing many native network tokens outside securities law. The FTC's endorsement duty does not depend on that question. It applies to any paid endorsement. This is not legal advice; route each brief through counsel for the markets the creator reaches.

Compare KOL deals with accountable alternatives too. Referral, affiliate or partner arrangements can tie payment to verified value, provided they guard against gaming and do not treat attributed wallets as unique customers. Our piece on [creator partnerships outside crypto](https://lowob.com/research/creator-partnerships-fintech-ai/) shows how fintech and AI firms structure them.

## lowob takeaways

- **Buy a defined behaviour.** Different goals need different creators, landing pages and measures.
- **Instrument before paying.** Without attribution through the wallet connection, you get a traffic report.
- **Judge on four stages.** Distribution, activation, durability and economics, with observed and inferred outcomes labelled.
- **Disclose by default.** Treat every paid post as an advertisement under FTC, FCA and MiCA rules.

## Common questions

### How do you measure a KOL campaign in crypto?

Track each creator through four stages: qualified distribution, attributed wallet activation, 7-day and 30-day retention, and full cost per verified activated user compared with other channels. Use unique links and carry campaign context through the wallet connection.

### What is a good cost per wallet for a crypto KOL campaign?

There is no reliable universal benchmark. Cost per activated wallet only means something alongside retention, wallet quality and deposit or usage value, and wallets are not unique people, so compare creators and channels on the same full-cost basis.

### Do crypto influencers have to disclose paid posts?

Yes in practice. The FTC requires clear and conspicuous disclosure of material connections, the SEC requires disclosure of compensation for promoting crypto asset securities, the UK FCA regulates crypto promotions, and MiCA requires marketing to be identifiable as such.

### Should KOL deals be paid upfront?

Test with a small first payment tied to delivery, and make renewals or larger payments conditional on activation and retention evidence. Where conversions can be verified, referral or affiliate terms can align payment with value.

## Next Move

Before approving another creator package, write down the behaviour it should produce, the link and wallet attribution that will record it, and the 30-day result that would justify a second payment. Add the disclosure wording to the brief.
